## Pick the draw animation by watching it, and two weapons that stopped taking each other down

The holster animation has been the same clip since 1.0, chosen by reading a name. This release
lets you watch every one of them on your own character and keep the one that reads — and fixes
a bug that had been quietly taking a second weapon off your body every time you drew the first.

### New

- **Gesture picker — pick a draw animation by watching it.** Dashboard → Placement → *Draw
  Style* → **Live Picker**. The panel steps aside, a camera frames your character, and every
  holster animation in the game plays on it at the press of a button. Keep the one you like per
  body slot, per direction. A gesture cannot be chosen by reading `weapons@holster_2h /
  unholster` — one of those strings is a man threatening someone, and it is what the pistol
  slot has been using.
- **The clip and its duration are now one decision.** Keeping an animation also stores how long
  it runs, measured from the clip itself. Every slot in this script has been playing a
  *fragment* of a longer animation — 19% of it for the pistol, 28% for the rifle — because the
  duration was tuned for a different clip years ago. Pick a new one and it plays whole.
- **`/mbt_animaudit`** (debug builds) measures every candidate animation against your game
  build: which exist, how long each runs, and which of your slots are cutting their animation
  short. The tedious half of choosing a gesture, done by the machine.
- **Per-job draw styles.** A style is a set of clips; jobs can be given their own. It changes
  the gesture and never the timing, so no job draws faster than another.
- **The second rifle now has a placed position** rather than one derived from an offset, tuned
  separately for male and female characters.

### Fixed

- **Drawing one of two weapons took both off your body.** With two rifles slung, equipping
  either one cleared the whole back until the next inventory sync put the other back. The equip
  path was asking the server to clear the *slot*, which was correct while a slot held one
  weapon and wrong from the moment it could hold two. It now reports what should still be
  there, so exactly one prop disappears and every player around you agrees on which.
- **Equipping a weapon whose prop was not on show did nothing at all.** If you drew during the
  half-second a prop takes to spawn, or while the weapon was concealed or hidden for your job,
  the equip went unrecorded — so putting it away never brought it back, and a prop that
  finished spawning stayed on your back with the weapon already in your hand.
- **The `ox_inventory` patch now updates when it changes.** Its marker was a number somebody
  had to remember to raise, and the first change that needed it did not get it: every server
  kept running the old fragment, and the Police draw style put the weapon away with the wrong
  animation. The marker is now a hash of the patch itself, so it can never go stale — and the
  patched file records which release wrote it.
- **`Hidden by Job` showed no jobs** on some servers while the same list rendered correctly
  elsewhere in the panel. Three separate parts of the dashboard were each fetching the job list
  on their own, with no retry; there is one fetch now, it retries, and if your framework really
  returns nothing the card says so instead of quietly offering one option.
- **A style removed from `default.lua` could make your config permanently unsavable.** Settings
  pointing at a style that no longer exists are now dropped instead of rejected.

### Changed

- **Draw Style moved to the Placement page.** Every card there opens an editor that hides the
  dashboard and puts you in front of your own character, which is what this one does too.
- The **Hidden by Job** card no longer leads with a red button that throws away every rule; it
  sits at the foot of the card, next to the sentence explaining what it discards.

### Note for server owners

**Restart the server after updating, not just the resource.** The `ox_inventory` patch changed,
so it is rewritten on start and `ox_inventory` has to recompile it.

Nothing needs configuring. Your existing draw animations are untouched — the picker changes
them only when you use it, and every setting persists to the database as before.

**Not tested this release:** the `qb-inventory` code path. The changes above are shared with
`ox_inventory` and were verified there. If you run qb-inventory and something looks wrong,
please open an issue — it will be fixed quickly.

### Install

Download `mbt_malisling.zip` below and drop it in your resources folder. Existing 2.0.x installs
upgrade in place — dashboard settings, placed racks, trunk contents and saved positions are all
kept.
